title: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
subtitle: Form, Structure, and Sense · 25 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **25 of the official questions in Form, Structure, and Sense are this one** — 1 Easy, 9 Medium, 15 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The sentence opens with a descriptive phrase that has no subject of its own, such as a participle phrase, 'After ___ing...', 'Compared to...', or 'Woven from...'.
- It ends in a comma and then the blank.
- The four choices are long clauses that say roughly the same thing but start with different nouns.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Ask who or what actually performed or is described by the opening phrase.
- 2) Find the choice whose first noun (its grammatical subject) is exactly that thing, not a related thing, its owner, or its maker.
- 3) Ignore how smooth the rest sounds.
- Only the first noun decides the answer.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices put a closely related noun first: the artist instead of the artwork, the object instead of its property, or the people affected instead of the people acting.
Some also start with 'when' or 'a/the X of...', which quietly moves the subject away from the phrase.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The wrong choices put a closely related noun first: the artist instead of the artwork, the object instead of its property, or the people affected instead of the people acting.
Some also start with 'when' or 'a/the X of...', which quietly moves the subject away from the phrase.
